questions.q: Two objects $AandB$ are placed at $15cmand25cm$ from the pole in front of a concave mirror having radius of curvature $40$ cm. The distance between images formed by the mirror is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let's consider the following diagram-

Let's assume that& ${v}_{A}, {v}_{B}$~indicates the distances of the images of objects A and B respectively.

Thus, by mirror formula, for object A, it can be written that

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} & = & \dfrac{1}{f} \\ \dfrac{1}{vA} + \dfrac{1}{- 15} & = & 1\left(- 20\right) \\ \dfrac{1}{vA} & = & \dfrac{1}{- 20} + \dfrac{1}{15} \\ = & \dfrac{- 3 + 4}{60} \\ {v}_{A} & = & 60cm\end{cases}$

Similarly, for object B, using mirror formula,

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{vB} + 1\left(- 25\right) & = & 1\left(- 20\right) \\ \dfrac{1}{vB} & = & \dfrac{- 1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{25} \\ & = & \dfrac{- 5 + 4}{100} \\ & = & \dfrac{- 1}{100} \\ {v}_{B} & = & - 100cm\end{cases}$

Hence, the distance~ \left(d\right)$~between the images can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}d & = & {v}_{A} + {v}_{B} \\ & = & \left(60 + 100\right)cm \\ & = & 160cm\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: Light travels in two media ${M}_{1}$ and ${M}_{2}$ with speeds $1 . 5 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$ and $2 . 0 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$ respectively. The critical angle between them is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Relative refractive index can be found as,

$\dfrac{\mu2}{\mu1} = \dfrac{v1}{v2} = \dfrac{1 . 5}{2} = \dfrac{3}{4}$.

When the angle of incident is greater than the critical angle total internal reflection occurs. If the critical angle is~${i}_{c}$~then,

$sin{i}_{c} = \dfrac{\mu2}{\mu1} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Now~$tan{i}_{c} = \dfrac{3}{{4}^{2} - {3}^{2}} = \dfrac{3}{7}$

Therefore,~${i}_{c} = \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{3}{7}\right)

$

questions.q: A ray of light $AO$ in vacuum is incident on a glass slab at angle $60 °$ and refracted at angle $30 °$ along $OB$ as shown in the figure. The optical path length of light ray from $A$ to $B$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Optical path length $= OA + \mu OB$
$= \dfrac{a}{cos{60}^{o}} + \dfrac{\mub}{cos{30}^{o}}$
$= 2a + \mu \left(\dfrac{2b}{\sqrt{3}}\right)
From Snell’s law,
$sin{60}^{o} = \musin{30}^{o}$
$\mu = $\sqrt{3}
Optical path length $= 2a + $\sqrt{3} \left(\dfrac{2b}{\sqrt{3}}\right)
$= 2 \left(a + b\right)$

$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_1}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_2}\right) \\ & \frac{1}{12}=(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{10}-\frac{1}{-15}\right) \\ & \frac{1}{12}=(\mu-1)\left(\frac{3+2}{30}\right) \\ & \mu=\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A prism of refractive index& $\mu$ and angle of prism~$A$ is placed in the position of minimum angle of deviation. If minimum angle of deviation is also $A$, then in terms of refractive,
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mu = \dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{A + {δ}_\min}{2}\right)}{sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

$\mu = \dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{A + A}{2}\right)}{sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

$\mu = \dfrac{sinA}{sin\dfrac{A}{2}} = 2cos\dfrac{A}{2}$

$A = 2\cos^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{μ}{2}\right)

$

questions.q: Diameter of the objective lens of a telescope is $250cm .$ For light of wavelength $600$ nm coming from a distant object, the limit of resolution of the telescope is close to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resolving limit of telescope $= \dfrac{1.22\lambda}{D}$
Where, $D$ = Diameter of lens
$\lambda$ = Wavelength of light
Resolving limit of telescope $= \dfrac{1.22 \times 600 \times 1{0}^{- 9}}{250 \times 1{0}^{- 2}} = 3 \times 1{0}^{- 7}$ rad

questions.q: The incident ray, reflected ray and the outward drawn normal are denoted by the unitvectors $\overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{b}$and~$\overset{→}{c}$ respectively. Then choose the correct relation for these vectors.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{a} = sin\theta\overset{^}{i} - cos\theta\overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{→}{b} = sin\theta\overset{^}{i} + cos\theta\overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{→}{c} = \overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{→}{a} - 2\left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right)\overset{→}{c} = sin\theta\overset{^}{i} + cos\theta\overset{^}{j}$

questions.q: The thickness at the centre of a plano convex lens is $3$ mm and the diameter is $6cm .$~If the speed of light in the material of the lens is $2 \times {10}^{8}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1} .$ The focal length of the lens is ___________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$R^{2} = r^{2} + ( R - t{)}^{2}$

$R^{2} = r^{2} + R^{2} + t^{2} - 2Rt$

Neglecting $t^{2},$~we get

$R = \dfrac{r2}{2t}$

$∴ \dfrac{1}{f} = \left(\mu - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{∞}\right) = \dfrac{\mu - 1}{R}$

$f = \dfrac{R}{\mu - 1} = \dfrac{r2}{2t ( \mu - 1 )} = \dfrac{\left(3 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)2}{2 \times 3 \times {10}^{- 3} \times \left(\dfrac{3}{2} - 1\right)}$

$= \dfrac{9 \times {10}^{- 4}}{6 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 1} \times 2$

$f = 0 . 3m = 30cm$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R)
Assertion (A) : Refractive index of glass is higher than that of air.
Reason ( $\mathrm{R}$) : Optical density of a medium is directly proportionate to its mass density which results in a proportionate refractive index.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: $(\mathrm{A})$ is not correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is correct
Both $(\mathrm{A})$ and $(\mathrm{R})$ are correct and $(\mathrm{R})$ is the correct explanation of (A)
$(A)$ is correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Refractive index has no relation with mass density because both have different meaning. Hence reason is incorrect.
So (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

questions.q:
There is a small source of light at some depth below the surface of water (refractive index $= \dfrac{4}{3}$ ) in a tank of large cross sectional surface area. Neglecting any reflection from the bottom and absorption by water, percentage of light that emerges out of surface is (nearly):
[Use the fact that surface area of a spherical cap of height $h$ and radius of curvature $r$ is $2\pirh$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$sin\beta = \dfrac{3}{4}, cos ⁡ \beta = \dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{4}$
Solid angle $dΩ = 2\piR^{2} \left($1 - cos ⁡ $\beta\right)
Percentage of light $= $\dfrac{2\piR^{2}\left(1 - cos ⁡ \beta\right)}{4\piR^{2}} \times$100$
$= $\dfrac{1 - cos\beta}{2} \times$100 = \left(\dfrac{4 - \sqrt{7}}{8}\right) \times$100 $\approx$17%$

questions.q: In normal adjustment, for a refracting telescope, the distance between objective and eye piece is $30$ cm. The focal length of the objective, when the angular magnification of the telescope is $2$, will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let& ${f}_{0}$~be the focal length of objective and~${f}_{e}$~is the focal length of eyepiece.

Given here,~${f}_{0} + {f}_{e} = 30$.

Angular magnification of telescope is given by~$m = \dfrac{f0}{fe}$.

So,~$2 = \dfrac{f0}{fe} ⇒ {f}_{0} = 2{f}_{e}$

Then, we have~${f}_{0} + \dfrac{f0}{2} = 30 ⇒ \dfrac{3{f}_{0}}{2} = 30$

Or,~${f}_{0} = 20cm$.

questions.q: A thin convex lens $L$ (refractive index $= 1.5$ ) is placed on a plane mirror $M$. When a pin is placed at $A$, such that $OA = 18cm,$ its real inverted image is formed at $A$ itself, as shown in figure. When liquid of refractive index ${\mu}_{l}$ is put between the lens and the mirror, the pin has to be moved to $A^{'},$ such that $OA^{'} = 27cm,$ to get its inverted real image at $A'$ itself. The value of ${\mu}_{l}$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{1}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{2}{18}$
$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{2}} = \dfrac{\left({\mu}_{1} - 1\right)}{- 18}$
When ${\mu}_{1}$ is filled between lens and mirror,
$P = \dfrac{2}{18} - \dfrac{2}{18}\left({\mu}_{1} - 1\right) = \dfrac{2 - 2{\mu}_{1} + 2}{18}$
$⇒ {F}_{m} = - \left(\dfrac{18}{2 - {\mu}_{1}}\right)
$2 = 6 - 3{\mu}_{1}$
$3{\mu}_{1} = 4$
${\mu}_{1} = \dfrac{4}{3}

questions.q: For the thin convex lens, the radii of curvature are at $15 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $30 \mathrm{~cm}$ respectively. The focal length the lens is $20 \mathrm{~cm}$. The refractive index of the material is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=\left(\frac{\mu_{\text {lens }}}{\mu_{\text {air }}}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_1}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_2}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{+20}=\left(\frac{\mu}{1}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{+15}-\frac{1}{(-30)}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{20}=(\mu-1)\left(\frac{3}{30}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mu-1=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \mu=1+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{3}{2}=1 \cdot 5\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Time taken by light to travel in two different materials $A$ and $B$ of refractive indices ${μ}_{A}$ and ${μ}_{B}$ of same thickness is ${t}_{1}$ and ${t}_{2}$ respectively. If ${t}_{2} - {t}_{1} = 5 \times {10}^{- 10}s$ and the ratio of ${μ}_{A}$ to ${μ}_{B}$ is $1: 2$. Then the thickness of material, in meter is: (Given ${v}_{A}$ and ${v}_{B}$ are velocities of light in $A$ and $B$ materials respectively).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The speed of light in a medium is inversely proportional to the refractive index of the material. Therefore,

$\dfrac{\muA}{\muB} = \dfrac{vB}{vA} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Let the thickness is $d$

$⇒ {t}_{2} - {t}_{1} = \dfrac{d}{vB} - \dfrac{d}{vA} = 5 \times {10}^{- 10}s$

As ${v}_{A} = 2{v}_{B} ⇒ d = 5 \times {10}^{- 10} \times 2{v}_{B}$

$⇒ d = 5 \times {10}^{- 10} \times {v}_{A}m$.&

questions.q: The refracting angle of a prism is $A$ and refractive index of the material of the prism is $cot \left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right).$Then the angle of minimum deviation will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, angle of minimum deviation is given by,& $⇒ \mu = \dfrac{sin\left({δ}_{m} + A\right)2}{sin\dfrac{A}{2}}$

$⇒ cot\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = \dfrac{sin\left({δ}_{m} + A\right)2}{sin\dfrac{A}{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{cos\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}{sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{sin\left({δ}_{m} + A\right)2}{sin\dfrac{A}{2}}$

$⇒ sin \left(90 ° - \dfrac{A}{2}\right) =sin \left(\dfrac{{δ}_{m} + A}{2}\right)

Therefore,~$90 ° - $\dfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{{δ}_{m} + A}{2}$⇒ {δ}_{m} = 180 ° - 2A$

$

questions.q:
In figure, the optical fiber is $l = 2m$ long and has a diameter of $d = 20\mum .$ If a ray of light is incident on one end of the fiber at angle ${\theta}_{1} = 40 °$ , the number of reflections it makes before emerging from the other end is close to:
(refractive index of fiber is $1.31$ , $sin40 ° = 0.64$ and $\sin^{- 1} ⁡ 0.49 = 30 °$ .)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let ${n}_{1}$~and~${n}_{2}$~be the refractive indices of the air and optical fibre respectively.~Applying Snell's law at Q, we get:

${n}_{1}sin{θ}_{1} = {n}_{2}sin{θ}_{2}$

$sin{40}^{∘} = 1 . 31 \times sin{θ}_{2}$

$⇒ sin{θ}_{2} = \dfrac{0 . 64}{1 . 31} = 0 . 4885 \approx 0 . 5$

$⇒ {θ}_{2} = {30}^{∘}$

The distance covered along the length of the optical fibre after one~reflection:

$QN = RN{cotθ}_{2}$

$= 20 \times {10}^{- 6} \times cot{30}^{∘} = 20\sqrt{3} \times {10}^{- 6}m$

The reflections~take place throughout~the length of the optical fibre.

Length of the wire$= 2m$

Total number of reflections along its length$= \dfrac{Lengthofthewire}{distancecoveredinonereflectionalongthelength}$

$= \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{6}}{20\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{100000}{3} = 57735 . 02 \approx 57000$

questions.q: An object is placed on the principal axis of convex lens of focal length $10$ cm as shown. A plane mirror is placed on the other side of lens at a distance of $20$ cm. The image produced by the plane mirror is $5$ cm inside the mirror. The distance of the object from the lens is ____ $cm$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here: Focal length of convex lens,& $f = 10cm$

Now, as seen in figure, image from lens is formed at point~${I}_{1}$, whose location is~$5$ cm~from mirror. Thus,~${I}_{1}$~is at~$15$ cm~from lens.

Using lens equation, we have

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

Putting the value,~

$\dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{- u} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{15} ⇒ u = \dfrac{10 \times 15}{10 - 15}$

Thus, object is placed at~$30$ cm& from lens.

questions.q: An object '$O$' is placed at a distance of $100$ cm in front of a concave mirror of radius of curvature $200$ cm as shown in the figure. The object starts moving towards the mirror at a speed $2cms^{- 1}$. The position of the image from the mirror after $10s$ will be at _____ $cm$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In& $10s$, the object will travel distance~$= 2 \times 10 = 20cm$

After $10sec$, the object will be at distance~$u = 20 - 100 = - 80m$.

Focal length of the concave mirror is $f = \dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{200}{2} = - 100cm$

Using mirror formula,

$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{v} = - \dfrac{1}{100} + \dfrac{1}{80} ⇒ v = \dfrac{8000}{20}$

$⇒ v = 400cm$

Position of image from the mirror is at~$400$ cm.

questions.q:
A container contains a liquid with refractive index of 1.2 up to a height of 60 cm and another liquid having refractive index 1.6 is added to height H above first liquid. If viewed from above, the apparent shift in the position of bottom of container is 40 cm. The value of H is ______ cm.
(Consider liquids are immisible)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$y=$ apparent depth of bottom
$\frac{\mathrm{y}}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{H}}{1.6}+\frac{60}{1.2}$
Shift $=40$
$H+60-y=40$
$\mathrm{H}+60-\frac{\mathrm{H}}{1.6}-\frac{60}{1.2}=40$
$\frac{6}{16} \mathrm{H}=30$
$\mathrm{H}=80 \mathrm{~cm}$
